question: Kým na Slovensku je na Štedrý večer kapor so šalátom, v ktorej ázijskej krajine si rodiny týždne vopred objednávajú vianočnú večeru z KFC?
source_excerpt: No Reservation, No Eat… KFC Becomes Japan's Traditional Christmas Food

extra.why_interesting: Slovak players assume Christmas dinner is a solemn family tradition (carp, potato salad); learning that an entire nation's equivalent is a bucket of fast-food chicken is a delightful 'really?!' moment. The Asian-country foothold plus the knowledge that Christmas isn't a religious holiday there lets players reason their way to Japan.
extra.verification_notes: KFC Christmas pre-order tradition in Japan is well documented (https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2022122313344230639); no contradicting or newer developments found.

explanation: Vďaka úspešnej reklamnej kampani KFC zo sedemdesiatych rokov sa vyprážané kura stalo v Japonsku vianočnou tradíciou. Pred pobočkami sa na Štedrý večer tvoria dlhé rady.

question: V indických reštauráciách McDonald's si hamburger z hovädzieho mäsa nekúpite. Prečo?
source_excerpt: the majority of Indians are Hindus who consider cows to be sacred.

extra.why_interesting: Players picture McDonald's as the same beef-burger chain everywhere; the idea of a McDonald's with no beef at all surprises, yet the cause is reasonable from general knowledge about India — an 'I can work this out' moment.
extra.verification_notes: McDonald's India avoids beef because most Indians are Hindus who consider cows sacred; no newer development contradicts this (csmonitor.com/1996/1017/101796.intl.intl.4.html).

explanation: Pre hinduistov, ktorí tvoria väčšinu Indov, je krava posvätné zviera. Indický náprotivok Big Macu, Maharaja Mac, sa preto robí z kuracieho mäsa.
